sections.name: UserController
sections.title: Profile read and update endpoints
sections.what: Defines the two endpoints a signed-in user uses to read and update their own profile.
sections.why: Likely reason: each user only reaches their own record, because the id comes from the login token.
sections.watch_out: Keep the user id taken from the token. Replacing it with an id from the request would expose other people's profiles.

summary: Exposes two web addresses that let a signed-in user read and update their own profile.
purpose: Lets the app fetch and change the profile of the person who is logged in.
why: Likely reason: keeps the controller thin and passes the real work to the service. Otherwise reason not stated in the code.
how: The read route takes the user id from the login token and returns that profile. The update route checks the request body against the update rules class and passes it to the service. Both routes sit under version 1 of the users path.
inputs: The login token supplies the user id. The update route takes a JSON body of profile fields.
outputs: Returns the profile wrapped in a data field, without the password hash.
risks: Access depends on the id coming from the token. If that ever changes to an id from the web address, users could read or edit other people's profiles. Body checks depend on a global validation setting that is not visible here.
debug: If the profile call returns a 401 error, check the login token. If the update returns a 400 error, check which field failed its rule. Database problems will show up in the user service.
